gen-luckiest-guy-fs-karma: Luckiest Guy shouts in blunt, marker-round strokes that never change width. Karma answers quietly, a text serif whose strokes thin gently between stem and hairline and whose terminals stop well short of the stem.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-ranade: Luckiest Guy sets a loud, high-cut line that looks poured at a single width, with the e opening clearly to the right. And Ranade spreads out beneath it in sans-serif curves that thin slightly at the turns, giving the loudness room to breathe.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans is wide-gapped and friendly, with curves that open freely. Against Luckiest Guy's tall, poured-ink lowercase, its moderate height makes the pair's strongest quality plain: a shout and a chat sharing one page.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-aclonica: Loud, cheerful and cut from strips. Luckiest Guy keeps every stroke one width, while Aclonica stretches out below in sans-serif lines with a deep midsection, so extended text moves along slowly and widely spaced.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-cascadia-code: Big, bright and blunt: Luckiest Guy holds a high line of poured, single-width ink. But Cascadia Code is wire-thin and widely spaced, so a smaller size for it would keep its open bends from drifting apart.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-cossette-texte: Cheerful from the first letter, Luckiest Guy sets a loud, high-cut line with an open-eyed e, and the stroke never varies. Cossette Texte reads smoothly, its wide-eyed e and prominent x-height carrying a long stretch easily.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-cossette-titre: Cossette Titre brings open bowls and nestled letters, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Luckiest Guy, loud and without thick-and-thin contrast, makes the pair's strongest quality a sharp split between shouting and smooth.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-kiwi-maru: Poured, single-width ink under a mean, high line. Luckiest Guy is built to shout, while Kiwi Maru, with generous letterspace and terminals far from the stem, is built to unfold slowly.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Loud ribbon-cut letters, cheerful and constant. Luckiest Guy stays tall and blunt, and Noto Sans Deseret answers with open apertures and a wide, squat lowercase, so the pair's strongest quality is how readily they separate.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Strokes like laser-cut sheet, one cutting width throughout. Luckiest Guy leads with that loud, high-set line, and Noto Sans Lisu follows with tiny ascender gaps and wide-open s curves that settle the page below it.
